newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW - GIO sees higher yr earnings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW - GIO sees higher yr earnings.

text.p: GIO Australia Holdings Ltd expects stronger earnings for the 12 months to June 30, 1997 but does not see second half earnings as strong as the first half, GIO managing director, Bill Jocelyn said on Wednesday.
Asked by Reuters in a telephone interview if GIO was confident of higher earnings in 1996/97 year, Jocelyn said: "I would certainly hope so but I wouldn't double the first half."
"Investment returns can't be that good in the second half," he said.

Jocelyn said on the business side he was still confident the business unit, which includes the general insurance and reinsurance divisions, would record double digit earnings growth in the 1996/97 financial year.

"There are good signs starting to emerge out of general insurance, particularly in respect of expenses - we got a reasonable result despite a pretty bad claims experience in the first six months," Jocelyn said.
GIO said earlier its general insurance results were hit by claims arising from major storms in Sydney and the New South Wales country towns of Armidale, Singleton and Coffs Harbour.
"I'm confident that our own changes (within the general insurance division) are starting to take effect, the removal of branches and telephone marketing," he said.
Jocelyn said GIO had been deliberately losing some business to improve the quality of its book.
He is concerned about the Compulsory Third Party (CTP) insurance business in Australia.
"I am worried about the underlying situation and the possibility of the claims escalating - I do have the uneasy feeling that the whole market is on feet of clay," he said.

GIO earlier posted a 22.3 percent increase in net profit to A$102.5 million for the six months to December 31. The company said earnings were lifted by buoyant conditions in both fixed interest and share markets.
The company warned that investment conditions were likely to be less buoyant in the second half but expected continued earnings growth for its non-investment business units.

Asked about current investment conditions for the Australian share market, Jocelyn said. "The question really is what happens to the American market. I think if you leave the American market out of the equation, the market looks OK."
Jocelyn said reinsurance premiums remained soft but were not as low as the company had expected.
